tasks.task: Implement deckcheck/curve.py::nonland_count(deck: Deck) -> int. Return the number of nonland card instances in the deck, respecting Entry counts and including commanders. See the docstring in the stub.
Implement deckcheck/curve.py::average_mana_value(deck: Deck) -> float. Mean mana value across nonland cards, respecting counts. Lands excluded. Return 0.0 if there are no nonlands.
Implement deckcheck/curve.py::curve_histogram(deck: Deck) -> dict[int, int]. Map integer mana value to nonland card count. X counts as 0, values of 7+ collapse to key 7, zero-count keys omitted.

Extend deckcheck/parse.py to handle three cases it currently mishandles: lines with a trailing collector number but no set code, names containing parentheses such as 'Erase (Not the Urza's Legacy One)', and MDFC names given only by their back face. Keep the existing parse() signature and do not break tests/test_parse.py.

Implement deckcheck/legality.py::check_deck_size(deck: Deck) -> list[Violation]. Commander decks are exactly 100 cards including commanders. A companion sits outside the 100. Return one Violation with rule='deck_size' if the count is wrong, otherwise an empty list.

Implement deckcheck/legality.py::check_singleton(deck: Deck) -> list[Violation]. At most one copy per name, exempting basic lands, names in the ANY_NUMBER set, and names in CAPPED up to their limit. One Violation per offending name with rule='singleton'.

Implement deckcheck/identity.py::color_identity(card: Card) -> frozenset[str] and identity_string(identity) -> str. Derive identity from mana_cost and oracle_text yourself; do NOT read card.color_identity. Handle hybrid, Phyrexian, all faces, and exclude reminder text in parentheses.

Implement deckcheck/legality.py::check_color_identity(deck: Deck) -> list[Violation]. Every card's identity must be a subset of the union of the commanders' identities. Use identity.color_identity, not the Scryfall field. rule='color_identity'. Note: identity.color_identity is itself an unimplemented stub - implement it (and identity_string, if your messages use it) as part of this task.

Implement deckcheck/legality.py::check_banlist(deck: Deck, banned: set[str]) -> list[Violation]. Flag cards whose lowercase name is in the passed-in set, falling back to Card.legalities['commander'] == 'banned'. Do not hardcode a banlist. rule='banned'.

Implement deckcheck/legality.py::check_commanders(deck: Deck) -> list[Violation]. Validate one or two commanders including all five partner variants: Partner, Partner with X, Choose a Background, Friends forever, Doctor's companion. The variants do not mix. Detect each from oracle_text and type_line. See the stub docstring.

Implement deckcheck/companions.py::check_companion(deck: Deck, companion: Card) -> list[Violation] and companion_name_map() -> dict[str, str], covering all nine companions. Each restriction is structurally different; read the stub docstring carefully, especially Jegantha and Zirda.

tasks.check: pytest -q tests/test_t11_companions.py -k "lurrus or obosh or gyruda or keruga or companion_itself"
tasks.task: Implement deckcheck/companions.py::check_companion(deck: Deck, companion: Card) -> list[Violation], covering four companions with mana-value restrictions: Lurrus of the Dream-Den (every PERMANENT card in the starting deck has mana value 2 or less; nonpermanents are unconstrained), Obosh, the Preypiercer (every NONLAND card has an ODD mana value), Gyruda, Doom of Depths (every NONLAND card has an EVEN mana value; note 0 is even), and Keruga, the Macrosage (every NONLAND card has mana value 3 or greater). The companion itself is never part of the deck it constrains. Do not implement the other five companions. See the stub docstring in deckcheck/companions.py.

Implement deckcheck/companions.py::check_companion(deck: Deck, companion: Card) -> list[Violation], covering two companions: Jegantha, the Wellspring (no card has more than one of the SAME mana symbol in its mana cost; {1}{R}{R} violates, {1}{W}{U} does not; hybrid and Phyrexian symbols count as the symbol they are written as - read this one carefully, it is the most commonly misimplemented) and Kaheera, the Orphanguard (every CREATURE card is a Cat, Elemental, Nightmare, Dinosaur, or Beast; a deck with no creatures satisfies it trivially). Do not implement the other seven companions. See the stub docstring in deckcheck/companions.py.

tasks.check: pytest -q tests/test_t11_companions.py -k "umori or zirda or yorion"
tasks.task: Implement deckcheck/companions.py::check_companion(deck: Deck, companion: Card) -> list[Violation], covering three companions: Umori, the Collector (every NONLAND card shares a card type; any one shared type suffices, and cards with multiple types can satisfy it via any of them), Zirda, the Dawnwaker (every PERMANENT card has an activated ability, written as 'cost: effect' in the rules text; beware colons that are not activated abilities, such as those inside keyword reminder text), and Yorion, Sky Nomad (the starting deck contains at least 20 cards more than the format minimum; in Commander that means 120 rather than 100). Do not implement the other six companions. See the stub docstring in deckcheck/companions.py.

Implement deckcheck/brackets.py::classify(deck, game_changers, combo_list) -> BracketReport. Classify 1-5 using the passed-in game changers set and combo list, plus detected mass land denial, extra-turn effects, and tutor density. Return 4 rather than guessing at 5 where the distinction is not mechanically decidable; record why in reasons. Note: find_combos in the same module is an unimplemented stub - if you call it, implement it as part of this task rather than assuming it works.

Implement deckcheck/brackets.py::find_combos(deck, combo_list) -> list[tuple[str,str]]. Return pairs from combo_list where both cards are present in the deck, matching case-insensitively by name, counting commanders as present, each pair once, in combo_list order.
